kind: Independent bounded application source review and direct-index stream controls

tests.expectation_method: Authored integer frame indices and exact dyadic samples/power-of-two gains; no production planner, quantizer, resampler or target execution supplies expectations. Quarter-second and power-of-two-clock coordinates avoid half-frame ambiguity.
controls: Different source/timeline rates 44100->48000 and48000->44100 copy exact raw sample bits at timeline-clock indices, with changed physical file-time consumption.
Multiple descriptors use distinct source rates 44100/192000/8000, independent gains, gaps and touching boundaries in one8192Hz timeline index space.
Partitions1/17/19/257/4096/8192/65536 as applicable and seeks across gap/start/end/8192 boundaries retain exact output suffixes.
Input-array and previously returned buffer mutations do not alter future fresh cursors.
Exact-capacity reads succeed; one-frame source overruns and a44100-source quarter-second at48000 timeline lacking12000 raw frames reject before stream publication.
Invalid source rates cannot be hidden by valid timeline rate; invalid requests leave cursor unchanged; raw signed zeros remain distinct from positive-zero gaps.

review_results.result: Segment retains an explicit sourceRate. The ordinary source accessor is constructed sourceRate/sourceRate, so source index seeks and reads remain unconverted. Stream/builder uses the separately supplied timelineRate. No implicit setter or conversion was inserted.

Fresh source clock replay, scalar length/offset computation and frozen unresolved source baseline remain unchanged. Explicit Rebase project.sampleRate selects new builder/reader context; the native original project clock is not claimed recovered. Playback still rereads source/media proof.

Construction bounds reader-quantized offset plus read extent against full verified source capacity. Per-call native read-result decision requires full completion. No missing-source tail padding is admitted; intentional timeline gaps remain zero.

One accessor remains active for the selected descriptor across blocks and is discarded on selection change. In this equal accessor-rate path there is no filter state. Stream progress publishes only after complete buffer success; invalid preflight requests do not advance.

This is an explicit source-event audition mode under the finite ordinary-reader context, not normal whole-project native playback. Remaining MIDI/plugin/routing/automation and arbitrary hosted provider state are not silently enabled.

resolved_findings.finding: New mode originally labeled canonical descriptor offset as media offset in seconds, which could be confused with actual file time when clocks differ.
resolved_findings.resolution: Root changed the new-mode caption to saved offset; final inspected UI source contains this wording. No numerical code changed for the correction.

limits: The static ordinary selector depends on explicit inactive scrub/ordinary state, sufficient channels and successful reader; arbitrary live providers or callbacks are not certified invariant.
The input stream is the admitted original complete source under fresh reconstruction; prepared/cache/warp replacement streams need their own rate/format ownership.
No Cubase executable, proprietary exporter or native runtime callback was executed.
These focused controls are application numerical and state validation; final full-suite, release identity and GUI observations are separate root-owned acceptance evidence.
No empirical pitch/frequency or device-output measurement was performed. Raw frame identity and output clock establish the stated numerical speed effect in this application.
